prompt: Some parents give their children everything that their children ask for or allow them to do whatever they want to do. Is this good for children?What could be consequences for these children when they grow up?
essay:
In modern society, some parents choose to satisfy all their children’s demands and give them complete freedom to do whatever they want. Although this parenting style may bring short-term happiness, I believe it is harmful to children’s long-term development and may lead to several negative consequences in adulthood.

On the one hand, constantly fulfilling children’s wishes may appear beneficial during childhood. When parents provide unrestricted freedom and excessive support, children are more likely to feel happy, confident, and emotionally satisfied. They may also experience less stress because they rarely face punishment or rejection at home. However, this parenting approach often prevents children from developing self-discipline and emotional resilience. Since they are not taught clear rules or boundaries, they may struggle to understand acceptable behaviour and become overly dependent on parental support. For example, when entering school, children who are rarely disciplined at home often find it difficult to follow classroom rules or cope with criticism from teachers and classmates.

More serious problems may emerge when these children grow up. One major consequence is that they may develop a strong sense of entitlement. Because they are accustomed to receiving everything they want, they may expect similar treatment from society, which can negatively affect their relationships with friends, colleagues, and even family members. In the workplace, for instance, they may become frustrated when supervisors reject their ideas or require them to follow strict rules. Another possible consequence is poor self-control. Children who are excessively indulged often fail to learn responsibility or patience, making it harder for them to manage pressure, control impulsive behaviour, or achieve long-term goals. In extreme cases, this may even increase the likelihood of antisocial behaviour.

In conclusion, while overindulgent parenting may make children feel happier in the short term, it is ultimately damaging because it weakens their ability to adapt to challenges and function responsibly in adult society.
